Both debaters agree on the value, and the arithmetic checks out. For the subgroups they assume, of orders p−1, p^{n−1}, and p^{n−1}(p−1), the sum is p^n + p − 1. Those orders are distinct for odd p and n ≥ 2, since p−1 < p ≤ p^{n−1}. Debater A's "(p + pⁿ) − 1" and Debater B's "p + pⁿ − 1" are the same expression, so the debate does not turn on wording.

The answer depends entirely on which three subgroups give almost commutative Terwilliger algebras. Neither debater derived that classification. Both took it from the solution, and A's justification ("natural candidates") is not a proof. Since Aut(G) is cyclic, it has a subgroup for every divisor of p^{n−1}(p−1), so the choice of the three is a real claim that needs support. I cannot confirm it from memory, so I can't certify p^n + p − 1 as correct.

Neither debater's argument establishes the answer, so neither is verified.

DECISION: NEITHER
